## Question 1: 

Generate a matrix of size $n\times n$ with the $ij$-th entry 
\[
\exp(-\theta(i-j)^2)
\]
Specify $n=10$ and $\theta=0.5$.

```{r}
theta <- 0.5
n <- 10
i <- matrix(rep(0:(n-1), each=n), n, n) # replicate from zero to 9
j <- matrix(rep(0:(n-1),n), n, n)
exp(-theta*(i-j)^2)

```




## Question 2: 

Use for loop and if statement to develop a function that can sort a vector of entries from the smallest to the largest. For example, you can implement the bubble sort algorithm. Bubble sort repeatedly looks at two neighboring items.

Bubble sort compares neighboring items from left to right. If the item on the left is larger than the item on the right, the two items are swapped. After the first pass, the largest unsorted item moves to the end. During the second pass, the algorithm starts again from the left but stops before the last sorted item. It repeats this process until no swaps are needed. 

The algorithm repeats this process until it completes a pass without making any swaps. At that point, the items are in ascending order.

For example, To sort 3, 7, 0, -5 in ascending order:

First pass

Compare 3 and 7: no swap.

Compare 7 and 0: swap and result 3, 0, 7, -5

Compare 7 and -5: swap and result 3, 0, -5, 7

Second pass

Compare 3 and 0: swap and result 0, 3, -5, 7

Compare 3 and -5: swap and result 0, -5, 3, 7

Third pass

Compare 0 and -5: swap and result -5, 0, 3, 7
Compare 0 and 3: no swap.

The sorted vector is:

-5, 0, 3, 7


Use your function to order the following vectors



```{r}
# # this is a function that take a vector v
bubble_sort <- function(v)
{  # look at bubble sort algorithm on youtube
    # calculate the length of array 
    n <- length(v)
             # run loop n-1 times
        for (i in 1 : (n - 1)) {
              # run loop (n-i) times
            for (j in 1 : (n - i)) {
                  # compare elements
                if (v[j] > v[j + 1]) {
                    update_val <- v[j]
                      v[j] <- v[j + 1]
                      v[j + 1] <- update_val
                }
            }
        }
      v
}

x <- c(5, 8, 9, 3, 2)
y <- c(4, 1, 8, 0, -3)

bbs_x <- bubble_sort(x)
bbs_y <- bubble_sort(y)
cat("The sorted vector for x is", bbs_x)
cat("\nThe sorted vector for y is ", bbs_y)


```
